title: The Customer Complaint System
overview: This specialized course addresses the complexities of managing customer complaints by focusing on two key components: the behavioral aspect, which pertains to how individual employees interact face-to-face with complainants, and the procedural aspect, which concerns the organization’s systematic approach to processing complaints from initiation to resolution. Drawing on ISO 10002 guidelines and other international best practices, the course also explores the cultural and organizational shifts necessary for effectively leveraging complaints, recovering dissatisfied customers, improving internal processes, and achieving greater customer satisfaction.
audience: This course is ideal for managers and staff responsible for customer complaint systems, customer service managers and teams, as well as managers and staff from support departments like HR and IT, who provide services to internal customers within the organization.
methodology: The course combines brief presentations by the consultant with group discussions, case studies, exercises, and hands-on activities such as designing procedures and forms in team settings, along with role-playing scenarios.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Advocate for the critical role of a customer complaints management system in driving organizational performance
Demonstrate how a well-trained employee can effectively handle customer complaints, build trust, and ensure customer satisfaction step by step
Implement a customer feedback system designed to maximize satisfaction and retention
Manage the entire complaint handling process, including preparation, receipt, analysis, escalation, tracking, and communication
Develop key performance indicators (KPIs) to evaluate and audit complaint management systems
